name: Biolith, Crystalworm
body:
This enormous worm is made of light blue crystal, and is covered with numerous, sharp spines.

Crystalworm Biolith
CR 12

XP 19,200
N Gargantuan outsider (earth, elemental, extraplanar)
Init -2 Senses darkvision 60 ft., tremorsense 60 ft.; Perception +18

AC 26, touch 4, flat-footed 28 (-2 Dex, +22 natural, -4 size)
hp 200 (16d10+112)
Fort +12; Ref +8; Will +9
Immune elemental traits

Speed 20 ft., burrow 20 ft., swim 10 ft.
Melee bite +25 (4d8+12/19-20 plus grab), gore +25 (2d8+12 plus bleed)
Space 20 ft.; Reach 15 ft.
Special Attacks bleed (1d8), swallow whole (4d8+18 bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage plus bleed, AC 21, 20 hp)

Str 35, Dex 6, Con 25, Int 1, Wis 8, Cha 8
Base Atk +16; CMB +32 (+36 grapple); CMD40 (can’t be tripped)
Feats Awesome Blow, Critical Focus, Improved Bull Rush, Improved Critical (bite), Power Attack, Staggering Critical, Weapon Focus (bite, gore)
Skills Perception +18, Swim +28

Environment any underground
Organization solitary
Treasure incidental

Crystalworm bioliths are enormous, crystalline beasts from the Elemental Plane of Earth. Sustained by a diet of rocks and minerals, crystalworms derive no nourishment from the flesh of other creatures. Despite this, crystalworms are notorious apex predators, attacking, swallowing, and killing other subterranean creatures as a display of aggression.

Fiercely territorial, a crystalworm often regurgitates shredded corpses in caverns at the edges of its territory, often the corpses of other dangerous predators, such as gugs. This tactic is intended to discourage visitors, and to lure scavengers that would otherwise be prowling the interior of the crystalworm’s territory to its perimeter, where they are free to feast upon the flesh of those who dared to disturb the crystalworm’s lair.
